circular-economy-acoustics.title: The Circular Economy: A New Era for Acoustic Solutions
circular-economy-acoustics.excerpt: How circular design principles are transforming the acoustic panel industry and why it matters for the future.

content.intro: The acoustic panel industry is undergoing a fundamental transformation. Traditional linear models—take, make, dispose—are giving way to circular approaches that keep materials in use indefinitely.

section1.title: Why Circularity Matters
section1.text: Every year, millions of tons of acoustic materials end up in landfills. These materials, often containing synthetic fibers and adhesives, can take centuries to decompose. The circular economy offers an alternative: designing products that can be continuously recycled.

section2.title: Our Approach
section2.text: At Re-Sound, we've designed our panels from the ground up for circularity. Using only recycled textiles and bio-based binders, our panels can be fully recycled at end of life—becoming new panels rather than waste.

content.quote: The best acoustic panel is one that never becomes waste.

section3.title: The Business Case
section3.text: Circular design isn't just good for the environment—it's good business. By creating value from waste and offering take-back programs, we build stronger relationships with customers while reducing material costs.

conclusion.title: Looking Forward
conclusion.text: The transition to circular acoustics is just beginning. As more companies adopt these principles, we'll see an industry transformed—one where acoustic comfort and environmental responsibility go hand in hand.

office-acoustic-solutions.title: Creating the Perfect Acoustic Environment in Modern Offices
office-acoustic-solutions.excerpt: Practical tips for improving acoustics in open-plan offices, meeting rooms, and collaborative spaces.

content.intro: Open-plan offices present unique acoustic challenges. Without proper treatment, noise levels can reduce productivity by up to 66%. Here's how to create a balanced acoustic environment.

section1.title: Understanding Office Acoustics
section1.text: Sound in offices comes from multiple sources: speech, equipment, HVAC systems, and external noise. Effective acoustic design addresses all these elements.

section2.title: Strategic Panel Placement
section2.text: Not all surfaces need treatment. Focus on ceiling areas above workstations, walls between collaborative and focused zones, and dividers between desks.

content.quote: Good acoustics is invisible—you only notice when it's missing.

section3.title: Balancing Absorption and Reflection
section3.text: Complete absorption creates an unnaturally 'dead' space. The goal is reducing reverberation while maintaining some natural ambience.

conclusion.title: Start Small, Measure Results
conclusion.text: Begin with high-impact areas and measure the difference. Often, strategic placement of a few panels can transform a space.

recycled-materials-quality.title: Recycled Materials: Meeting and Exceeding Quality Standards
recycled-materials-quality.excerpt: How we ensure our recycled textile panels match or exceed the performance of traditional materials.

content.intro: There's a persistent myth that recycled materials mean compromised quality. Our panels prove the opposite—recycled can mean superior.

section1.title: Rigorous Material Selection
section1.text: Not all recycled textiles are suitable for acoustic panels. We carefully select and sort materials to ensure consistent fiber quality and acoustic performance.

section2.title: Advanced Processing
section2.text: Our proprietary processing transforms mixed textiles into uniform acoustic fiber. This consistency is key to achieving predictable, high-performance results.

content.quote: Sustainability and quality aren't trade-offs—they're complements.

section3.title: Third-Party Testing
section3.text: Every batch undergoes acoustic testing to EN ISO 354 standards. We achieve Class A absorption ratings consistently, meeting the same standards as virgin material panels.

conclusion.title: The Future is Recycled
conclusion.text: As processing technology improves, recycled materials will increasingly outperform virgin alternatives. The question isn't whether to use recycled—it's how quickly we can scale.

sound-absorption-explained.title: Sound Absorption Explained: A Guide for Architects
sound-absorption-explained.excerpt: Everything you need to know about sound absorption coefficients and selecting the right panels.

content.intro: Understanding acoustic specifications can be challenging. This guide breaks down the key metrics and what they mean for your project.

section1.title: The αw Coefficient
section1.text: The weighted sound absorption coefficient (αw) is the most common metric. It ranges from 0 (no absorption) to 1 (complete absorption). Our panels achieve αw 0.95-1.00.

section2.title: Frequency Considerations
section2.text: Different materials absorb different frequencies. Porous materials like ours excel at mid and high frequencies—the speech range—making them ideal for offices.

content.quote: The right absorption depends on the room's purpose.

section3.title: Coverage Calculations
section3.text: More isn't always better. The ideal coverage depends on room volume, surface materials, and intended use. We offer free acoustic consultations to help specify correctly.

conclusion.title: Beyond the Numbers
conclusion.text: While specifications matter, the best acoustic design considers the whole experience. Aesthetics, sustainability, and wellbeing all contribute to successful spaces.

acoustics.title: Sound absorption
acoustics.intro: PET felt is a porous absorber: sound enters the open fibre structure and is turned into heat. How much a panel absorbs depends on its thickness and, above all, on how it is mounted. Fixed straight to the wall it treats mainly mid and high frequencies; with an air cavity or mineral wool behind it, absorption rises sharply and reaches lower frequencies.

absorptionVsInsulation.question: What is the difference between sound absorption and sound insulation?
absorptionVsInsulation.answer: Sound absorption and sound insulation solve different problems. Absorption reduces echo and reverberation inside a room by converting sound-wave energy into heat as it strikes a soft, porous material — that's what every Re-Sound panel does. Insulation prevents sound from passing through a wall or floor into the next room, which requires dense, sealed mass construction. Re-Sound panels improve the acoustics of the space you are in; they are not a soundproofing solution between rooms.

whatIsReverberation.question: What is reverberation and why does it matter?
whatIsReverberation.answer: Reverberation is the persistence of sound in a room after the original source has stopped — the "live" quality of a hard-surfaced room. It is measured as RT60: the time it takes a sound to fall by 60 decibels. High reverberation makes speech difficult to understand, raises ambient noise levels, and increases listener fatigue. In offices, restaurants, schools and healthcare environments the recommended RT60 is typically between 0.4 and 0.8 seconds. Re-Sound panels reduce reverberation by absorbing mid- and high-frequency sound — the range where human speech lives.

whatInfluencesAcoustics.question: What influences the acoustics of a room?
whatInfluencesAcoustics.answer: Three things drive room acoustics: the volume of the space, the materials on its surfaces, and the function it serves. Hard, smooth surfaces (concrete, glass, tile, parquet) reflect sound and create echo. Soft, porous surfaces (textiles, recycled-fibre panels, carpet) absorb it. The larger and harder a space is, the more absorptive surface you need to bring reverberation down to a comfortable level. Re-Sound panels are designed to add that absorptive surface without adding bulk.

whatIsAlphaW.question: What do αw, NRC, and Class A mean on the spec sheets?
whatIsAlphaW.answer: They are different ways of expressing the same property: how much sound a material absorbs. αw is the weighted sound absorption coefficient defined by ISO 11654 — a single number from 0 (perfect reflector) to 1.0 (perfect absorber). NRC (Noise Reduction Coefficient, ASTM C423) is the American equivalent, also 0 to 1.0. Class A is the top absorption class in ISO 11654, awarded to materials with αw ≥ 0.9. Several Re-Sound products are Class A rated: the higher the αw, the more absorptive the panel.

howManyPanels.question: How many panels do I need for my space?
howManyPanels.answer: As a rule of thumb, plan for absorptive surface equivalent to about 20-30% of the floor area in a typical office, meeting room or restaurant. So a 30 m² room will benefit from roughly 6-9 m² of acoustic panels. The exact figure depends on existing surfaces, ceiling height, and the use case — for a more precise number we are happy to run a Sabine calculation based on your floor plan. Send us the dimensions and we will come back with a recommendation.

whereCanUse.question: Where can Re-Sound panels be used?
whereCanUse.answer: Re-Sound panels are designed for B2B interior environments: offices, meeting rooms, open-plan workspaces, lobbies and reception areas, restaurants, hotels, schools and universities, healthcare facilities, libraries, and cultural spaces. They can be wall-mounted, ceiling-mounted or freestanding (Divide), and the wood-veneer ranges (rWood) are suitable for premium, design-led architectural projects where appearance matters as much as performance.

rwoodVsRpetVsTextile.question: What is the difference between rWood, rPET and the textile range?
rwoodVsRpetVsTextile.answer: They are three different material families serving different design intents. The textile range (Interior, Solid, Divide) is made from recycled textile fibres (at least 80 % recycled content) with a fabric cover — soft, warm, available in multiple colours, manufactured in our own plant in Beveren-Waas (Belgium). The rPET range (Panel, Groove, Flex Groove) is made from recycled PET bottles (rPET Panel and rPET Flex Groove are made entirely from recycled PET), OEKO-TEX® certified, and can be processed like MDF (cut, mill, paint); ideal for bold colours and custom installations. The rWood range (Groove, Perf, Micro, Panel) combines FSC-certified wood veneer with a recycled-felt core, giving a premium architectural finish in 8+ wood species; manufactured in our own plant in Częstochowa (Poland).

fireSafety.question: What fire safety classifications do Re-Sound panels carry?
fireSafety.answer: Fire classification varies by product line. The rPET range is certified B-s1,d0 to EN 13501-1 — suitable for most commercial and public-building applications. The rWood range carries classifications up to B-s2,d0 depending on finish, and the micro-perforated rWood Micro reaches the highest fire safety rating in our catalog. Each product page lists the exact certification, and the test certificates are available as PDF downloads after a quick contact form. For specific project compliance requirements get in touch with the exact classification you need.

samples.question: Can I order samples?
samples.answer: Yes — samples are free for qualified B2B requests. Use the contact form on any product page to request samples; specify which colours, finishes or veneers you would like to see. Sample kits are typically shipped within 5 working days within the EU. For larger projects we can also arrange a showroom visit or send a project consultant on site.

whatIsCircular.question: What does "circular" mean at Re-Sound?
whatIsCircular.answer: Circular at Re-Sound means three things, designed in from the start. First, inputs: we use recycled materials wherever the acoustic performance allows it — recycled textile fibres (at least 80 % recycled content) in the Interior/Solid/Divide range, recycled PET bottles in the rPET range (rPET Panel and rPET Flex Groove are made entirely from recycled PET), and a recycled-felt core under the FSC-certified veneer of the rWood range. Second, end of life: every Re-Sound panel can be returned to us through our free take-back service, and the materials are reprocessed into new panels or new raw material rather than going to landfill. Third, design: connections (magnetic, mechanical, hook systems) are reversible so panels can be removed without destruction, allowing reconfiguration during the building's life.

takeBack.question: How does the take-back program work?
takeBack.answer: At end of life — when a building is being refurbished or the panels are being replaced — Re-Sound will collect the panels from your site, free of charge within Belgium and at logistics cost in the rest of the EU. We then process them back into raw material: textile panels are shredded and re-spun into new fibre; rPET panels are reground and re-pressed; rWood cores are separated from the veneer and reused. To initiate a return, contact us with the original delivery reference and approximate volume.

recycledContent.question: What is the recycled content of each product line?
recycledContent.answer: Recycled content varies by product family. The textile range (Interior, Solid, Divide) is made from recycled textile fibres with high recycled content. The rPET range uses post-consumer recycled PET; rPET Panel and rPET Flex Groove are made entirely from recycled PET (the actual bottle-equivalent count varies by panel size — roughly 60 bottles per standard Groove panel). The rWood range uses a high recycled-fibre core with FSC-certified veneer on the visible face. Detailed material breakdowns and EPD documentation are available on each product page and on request.

leadTimes.answer: Standard catalog items ship within 2-3 weeks from order confirmation across the EU. Custom sizes, custom colours, or large project quantities typically run 4-6 weeks. For projects on a deadline, contact us with the timeline and we will confirm what is achievable before order placement.

rpet.h1: PET acoustic panels: rPET Panel, Groove and Flex Groove
rpet.intro: PET acoustic panels turn post-consumer bottles into a dense polyester felt that absorbs sound, takes a CNC cutter like MDF and comes in a colour palette architects actually use. Re-Sound is a Stretch Group brand. We manufacture in our own plants in Beveren-Waas (Belgium) and Częstochowa (Poland); the rPET range is produced in Częstochowa. The range has three models. rPET Panel is the flat sheet: cut it, mill it, drill it and paint it for walls, ceilings and furniture. rPET Groove adds a grooved surface in 12 colours and three thicknesses for higher absorption on walls and ceilings. rPET Flex Groove keeps the grooved look but bends around columns and curved walls down to a 500 mm radius. All three are OEKO-TEX® Standard 100 certified, reach B-s1,d0 or B-s2,d0 under EN 13501-1 and can be taken back for recycling at end of life. Use the table below to compare PET acoustic panels by format, absorption and lead time, then open the model page for finishes and downloads.
rpet.whyCertsDesc: Every rPET model is OEKO-TEX® Standard 100 certified; fire certificates (EN 13501-1) are on the model pages.

q1.question: Are PET acoustic panels really made from recycled bottles?
q1.answer: Yes. The felt is made from post-consumer PET bottle fibre: rPET Panel and rPET Flex Groove are made entirely from recycled PET, and rPET Groove is made from the same recycled PET felt. Every model is OEKO-TEX® Standard 100 certified, so the material is suitable for schools and healthcare.

q2.question: How much sound do PET acoustic panels absorb?
q2.answer: It depends on thickness and mounting: rPET Groove reaches NRC 0.55 (12 mm), 0.75 (24 mm) and 0.90 (36 mm); rPET Panel reaches up to αw 1.00 when mounted on a frame with an air cavity. Panels glued directly to the wall absorb less than panels with a cavity behind them.

q3.question: What fire class do recycled PET acoustic panels have?
q3.answer: rPET Groove and rPET Flex Groove are classified B-s1,d0 under EN 13501-1; the rPET Panel spec sheet states B-s2,d0. The fire certificate for each model is on its downloads block.

q4.question: Can I cut and paint PET acoustic panels on site?
q4.answer: Yes. rPET Panel behaves like MDF: cut, mill, drill and screw it with standard tools, and paint it in any RAL or NCS colour. The grooved panels are cut to size on site with a fine-tooth blade.

q5.question: What is the lead time for PET acoustic panels?
q5.answer: Stock colours ship in 2–3 weeks from our Częstochowa plant; custom colours take 5–6 weeks. Large projects are scheduled in production batches — ask us for a binding date before you order.

rwood.title: Wood Acoustic Panels — Veneer, Perforated & Micro-perforated | Re-Sound
rwood.description: Wood acoustic panels in FSC veneer: grooved (Groove), micro-perforated (Micro), perforated (Perf) and smooth (Panel). αw up to 0.90, B-s1,d0 FR core.
rwood.h1: Wood acoustic panels in FSC veneer: grooved, perforated, micro-perforated, smooth
rwood.intro: Wood acoustic panels bring a real veneer surface to walls and ceilings without giving up absorption. Re-Sound is a Stretch Group brand. We manufacture in our own plants in Beveren-Waas (Belgium) and Częstochowa (Poland). The rWood range covers four surfaces on one construction principle: an FSC-certified veneer over an acoustic core. rWood Groove is the linear slat look with oak and walnut veneers on a felt backing (αw 0.90). rWood Micro drills 0.5 mm micro-perforations through the veneer, so the wood reads as a closed surface while the panel absorbs (αw 0.90, B-s1,d0). rWood Perf uses visible perforation patterns with 5 to 8 mm holes, tuned between αw 0.35 and 0.85. rWood Panel is the smooth veneered sheet for areas where the wood, not the acoustics, leads. Eight veneers run across the range, from Beech White Ash to Tobacco Walnut. Compare wood acoustic panels below by format, absorption, fire class and lead time, then open a model page for finishes and downloads.
rwood.whyCertsDesc: FSC®-certified veneer on every rWood model; rWood Panel additionally has an EPD available on request.

q1.question: Which wood acoustic panel absorbs the most?
q1.answer: rWood Groove and rWood Micro both reach αw 0.90 with a felt or mineral-wool backing. rWood Perf ranges from αw 0.35 (PH5) to 0.85 (PD8) depending on the perforation pattern. rWood Panel is a smooth veneered board chosen for its look rather than its absorption.

q2.question: Is the veneer on wood acoustic panels FSC-certified?
q2.answer: Yes — every rWood model uses FSC®-certified veneer, and rWood Panel also has an EPD available on request. Chain-of-custody documentation is available for tenders.

q3.question: What fire class do wood acoustic panels achieve?
q3.answer: With the fire-retardant (FR) MDF core the rWood models are classified B-s1,d0 under EN 13501-1; on a standard MDF core the classification is D-s2,d0. Specify the FR core for escape routes and public buildings.

q4.question: Can micro-perforated wood panels be backlit?
q4.answer: Yes — rWood Micro is available with a backlit option: the 0.5 mm perforations let light through while the surface still reads as solid wood.

q5.question: How are wood acoustic panels mounted, and what is the lead time?
q5.answer: All models mount on a concealed clip system (or glue-fixing for permanent installations); rWood Groove can also be fixed to battens with tongue-and-groove joints. Stock veneers ship in 3–4 weeks; non-stock species and custom finishes in 6–8 weeks.

booths.h1: Office phone booths and meeting pods from the manufacturer
booths.intro: An office phone booth gives one person a quiet, ventilated place for calls and video meetings inside an open-plan floor; a meeting pod does the same for a team. Re-Sound's booths are manufactured in our own plant in Częstochowa (Poland), delivered and installed by our own team at fixed prices within mainland Europe, with a 5-year structural warranty (Solo ECO: 5-year spare-part warranty). The booth range has four models. Solo ECO is the entry model: a one-person booth with a standing table, a country-specific socket with USB-A and USB-C (socket only for Denmark), ventilation up to 4 m³/min and a closed or glass back wall. Solo Flex is the one-person office phone booth: a 1 m² footprint, a sit-stand desk, 230 V and USB-C power, silent EC fans and a 24 dB(A) speech level reduction measured under ISO 23351-1. Duo is the two-person acoustic phone booth with two configurations — Flex for a two-seat conversation, Work for one person with a full-width desk. Modular XL is the acoustic meeting pod for six to ten people: the base unit extends in 90 cm segments and reaches 25.9 dB(A) speech level reduction. Solo Flex, Duo and Modular XL carry the 5-year structural warranty and Solo ECO the 5-year spare-part warranty; all four are delivered EU-wide. q1.question: How much quieter is an office phone booth?
q1.answer: Speech level reduction is measured under ISO 23351-1: Solo Flex reaches about 24 dB(A) and Modular XL 25.9 dB(A), both Class C under the standard (A+ ≥ 33, A ≥ 30, B ≥ 27, C ≥ 24, D ≥ 21 dB(A)). In a typical open-plan office that keeps a normal call from being intelligible outside the booth.

q2.question: Do acoustic phone booths need a power connection?
q2.answer: Yes — each booth plugs into a standard 230 V socket for lighting, ventilation and the desk outlets (Schuko plus USB-C PD 60 W). Solo Flex draws about 80 W in use. Solo ECO has one country-specific socket with USB-A and USB-C (socket only on the Danish version) and draws 22 W in use.

q3.question: How is a privacy pod ventilated?
q3.answer: Silent EC fans exchange the air continuously — 4.6 m³/min in Solo Flex, 9.2 in Duo and 18.4 in the Modular XL base unit — controlled by an occupancy sensor so the booth is fresh when someone walks in.

q4.question: Which meeting pod fits six people or more?
q4.answer: Modular XL: the base unit seats six and each 90 cm segment adds capacity up to ten, with A/V provisions and a wide step-free door.

q5.question: What are the lead time and warranty for a phone booth?

Solo Flex and Duo ship 4–6 weeks from order, Modular XL 6–8 weeks for the base unit; custom fabrics add 2–3 weeks. hero.title: Reverberation time calculator
hero.subtitle: Enter the dimensions and finishes of your room to estimate its RT60, compare it with the target for the room type and find out how many m² of acoustic panels bring it within range.

intro.title: Sabine's formula and the targets
intro.sabine: The calculator uses Sabine's formula in the form T = V / (6 × A): T is the reverberation time in seconds, V the room volume in m³ and A the total absorption in m² sabine — every surface area multiplied by its absorption coefficient α, added up. Each octave band from 125 Hz to 4000 Hz is calculated separately with the α values of the selected floor, ceiling and wall finishes.
intro.headline: The headline RT60 is the mean of the 500, 1000 and 2000 Hz bands — the speech frequencies — and that is the value compared with the target.
intro.targets: The target reverberation times per room type come from the same source table as the absorption coefficients: from 0.4 s for a music studio to 1.5 s for a sports hall or swimming pool; an office, meeting room or classroom aims for 0.8 s.
intro.note: Sabine's formula assumes the absorption is spread evenly over the room. The result is an estimate for early design decisions, not a measurement.

officeTarget.question: What reverberation time should an office have?
officeTarget.answer: The target table used by this calculator sets 0.8 s for an office, meeting room, classroom, nursery and living room, 0.7 s for a call centre, restaurant or café or bar, and 1.0 s for a reception or waiting room. The calculator shows whether your estimated RT60 meets the target for the room type you select.

hardFinishes.question: Which finishes absorb the least sound?
hardFinishes.answer: In the table, marble has an absorption coefficient of 0.01 in every octave band, concrete 0.01 to 0.03 and plaster 0.01 to 0.05. Soft finishes absorb far more: carpet reaches 0.37 at 4000 Hz and heavy curtains 0.96 at 500 Hz. A room with hard finishes on the floor, ceiling and walls therefore has a long reverberation time.

howManyM2.question: How many m² of acoustic panels do I need?
howManyM2.answer: The calculator works out the extra absorption in m² sabine that brings the headline RT60 — the mean of the 500, 1000 and 2000 Hz bands — down to the target, then divides it by the weighted absorption coefficient αw of each Re-Sound panel with a published single value: 1 m² of a panel with αw 1.0 adds 1 m² sabine. Panels whose αw depends on the pattern or thickness are listed without a quantity and link to their product page.
